geometry.note: This is the SURFACE building only, per its own OSM name. The NOvA near detector is '100 m underground' (src:nova-arxiv-2025-monopole-search) and 'located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target'; its horizontal offset from this surface point is not sourced, so the underground detector is not drawn separately. Release pass (gaps stream): the earlier distance check against a derived NuMI target (964.9 m vs 1 km, which had raised this to verified) was removed, because the NuMI target now sits at its surveyed position (NuMI TDR beam sheet) and this building stands 861 m from it, on the beam axis (0.8 m off), i.e. about 140 m upstream of the 1 km at which the detector sits: it is the shaft building, not the detector.

notes: QA pass (2026-09-21): removed the `valid: {start: '2014-02-06', end: null}` window a previous pass set -- a preventive fix for a latent bug in hepgraph.atlas.build._feature_segments(): any `valid` dict with a non-null `start` and `end: null` hard-codes `status: 'active'` through build day regardless of the entity's real status, bypassing state_segments entirely. Currently harmless because detector:nova-near-detector genuinely is 'active' today, but this pattern produced a live false-'active' claim on three other records (geometry:lhc-tunnel-ring, geometry:fermilab-mc1-building, geometry:fermilab-microboone-hall) fixed the same way in this pass -- see docs/atlas-worklog/REVIEW_geometry_qa.md.

Release pass (gaps stream): confidence lowered from verified to approximate and the distance check removed; see geometry note. The building lies 861 m from the surveyed NuMI target (TDR beam sheet) and 75 m from the MINOS surface building.
